title: Split Digraphs and Magic E
keyIdea: A split digraph is two letters that make one vowel sound with another letter in between them: the vowel and an e at the end of the word. Put an e on the end of cap and you get cape: the e is silent, but it makes the a say its name. The five split digraphs are a–e (cake), e–e (these), i–e (bike), o–e (home) and u–e (cube, tune). When you count the sounds in a word like cake, the a–e counts once: c, a–e, k is 3 sounds in 4 letters.
familyTip: Write cap, kit, hop and cub on scraps of paper and make one small card with an e on it. Take turns sliding the e onto the end and reading the new word out loud: cape, kite, hope, cube. Then hunt for split digraph words on food boxes and signs, like cake, bike, home or June, and draw a little bridge from the vowel over to the e.

visual.caption: Short vowel or long vowel? Drag each word, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag the magic e onto a word, join the split digraph, count sounds not letters, fix the word that lost its e, sort short from long vowels.

kid: Look at the word cap. Now put an e on the end. It says cape! The e makes no sound. But it makes the a say its name.
The a and the e are a team. They make one sound, even with the p between them. We call this a split digraph. Split means the two letters are apart.
There are five of them: a–e in cake, e–e in these, i–e in bike, o–e in home, and u–e in cube.
When you count sounds, the team counts as one. Cake has four letters. But it has three sounds: c, a–e, k. With no e, the vowel is short, like in tap. With the e, it is long, like in tape.
adult: Ages 5 to 7. The National Curriculum in England (English Appendix 1, Year 1) lists the split digraphs a–e, e–e, i–e, o–e and u–e among the graphemes children should read and spell, with examples such as made, these, five, home and rule. CCSS RF.1.3c asks first graders to know the final -e convention for long vowel sounds. Key terms: split digraph, grapheme, phoneme, short vowel, long vowel, consonant.

The rule taught here: when a single vowel is followed by one consonant and a final e, the e is silent and the vowel takes its long sound, often described as saying its name. The two letters are one grapheme for one phoneme, even though a consonant sits between them, so cake is 4 letters but 3 phonemes. u–e has two long sounds: /yoo/ as in cube and /oo/ as in rule or June; some speakers also say tune with /yoo/.

Common mistakes: sounding the final e out loud (kit-ee); counting each letter as a sound (cake as 4 sounds); reading a split digraph word with a short vowel, so hope is read as hop; leaving the e off in spelling, which can make a different real word (kit for kite); and confusing a split digraph with vowels side by side, such as oa in road. Be careful with common exception words like have, give, come and love, where the final e does not make the vowel long; English words rarely end in v, so the e is there for spelling.

In the lab your child drags an e onto cap, kit, hop and cub and sees the new word, taps the vowel and the e that make one sound, counts sounds in cake, bike, slide and home, finds the word in a sentence that should have an e, and sorts short and long vowel words. Each wrong tap gets a short reason. Phonics programmes may call it magic e, split digraph or vowel-consonant-e; it is the same idea.

practice.prompt: Put an e on the end of hop. What word do you get?
practice.hint: Keep the same letters and add e at the very end.
practice.explain: hop + e = hope. The e makes the o say its name.

practice.prompt: Sam writes {n} words that have a magic e, like cake. How many silent e letters did Sam write?
practice.hint: Each magic e word has one silent e at the end.
practice.explain: One silent e in each word, so {n} words have {n} silent e letters.

practice.prompt: How many sounds are in bike?
practice.hint: Say it slowly. Do i and e make one sound together?
practice.explain: b, i–e, k: the i–e is one sound, so bike has 3 sounds and 4 letters.

practice.prompt: A word has {n} letters and one split digraph. Every other letter makes its own sound. How many sounds does it have?
practice.hint: The vowel and the end e make just one sound together.
practice.explain: The two letters of the split digraph count as one sound, so {n} letters make {=n-1} sounds.

practice.prompt: Which word has a split digraph?
practice.hint: Look for a vowel, one letter, then an e at the end.
practice.explain: In home, o and e make one sound with the m in between: h, o–e, m.

pool.prompt: What sound does the e at the end of cake make?
pool.hint: Say cake. Do you hear an e at the end?
pool.explain: The final e is silent. Its job is to make the a say its name.

pool.prompt: Which word says the long a, like in its name?
pool.hint: Look for the magic e on the end.
pool.explain: tape has a–e, so the a says its name. tap has no e, so its a is short.

pool.prompt: In tune, which letters make one sound together?
pool.hint: Find the vowel and the e at the end.
pool.explain: u and e are a split digraph with the n in between: t, u–e, n.

pool.hint: To fly it, the i needs to say its name.
pool.explain: kite needs the i–e split digraph. A kit is a set of things, not something you fly.

pool.prompt: Mia reads {n} words. Each one has a split digraph. How many vowels say their name?
pool.hint: Each split digraph makes one vowel say its name.
pool.explain: One long vowel in each word, so {n} vowels say their name.

pool.prompt: Which word does NOT have a split digraph?
pool.hint: In a split digraph, one letter sits between the vowel and the e.
pool.explain: In road, o and a sit side by side, so it is not a split digraph. rode and rope have o–e.

pool.prompt: Tom has {n} cards: cap, kit, hop and more. He puts an e on the end of each. How many new words can he read?
pool.hint: Each card plus an e makes one new word.
pool.explain: Each of the {n} cards becomes one new word, like cap to cape, so that is {n} new words.

pool.prompt: How many sounds are in slide?
pool.hint: Say it slowly: s, l, then the long i, then d.
pool.explain: s, l, i–e, d is 4 sounds in 5 letters.

pool.prompt: Which pair shows a magic e changing a word?
pool.hint: Find the pair where only an e is added.
pool.explain: cub + e = cube: the e makes the u say its name.
